brief.headline: HBM supercycle intact; DRAM +58-63% QoQ Q2, NAND +70-75%; hyperscaler capex ~$700B; CoWoS gap narrows to 10% by year-end
brief.summary: <cite index="22-5,22-9">The four biggest hyperscalers will spend roughly $700 billion on capital expenditures in 2026</cite>, doubling YoY, with <cite index="22-4,27-3">2027 estimates now exceeding $1 trillion</cite>. <cite index="11-7,15-15">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 90-95% QoQ in Q1 and are projected to climb 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, while NAND Flash will jump 70-75% QoQ</cite>, driven by AI infrastructure demand and <cite index="6-1">Goldman Sachs forecasting a 4.9% DRAM supply deficit in 2026</cite>. <cite index="32-4,32-6">TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap is expected to narrow from 20% to 10% by end-2026 as monthly capacity reaches 120,000-140,000 wafers</cite>, with <cite index="31-3,35-1">Nvidia securing roughly 60% of total CoWoS allocation for 2026</cite>. <cite index="4-2,4-3">Samsung posted Q1 2026 semiconductor operating profit of 53.7 trillion won ($36.1B), while SK Hynix reported 52.6 trillion won revenue and 37.6 trillion won operating profit</cite>, fueled by HBM sales.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="40-7,40-10">Foreign investors poured 3.1 trillion won into SK Hynix over four trading days, narrowing the market-cap gap with Samsung to 2.5x (173T vs 430T won), the closest in history</cite>. <cite index="40-17,40-19">SK Hynix effectively monopolizes HBM3E supply for Nvidia Blackwell, while Samsung struggles to enter the HBM supply chain</cite>. <cite index="5-11">Q4 2025 HBM market share: SK Hynix 57%, Samsung 22%, Micron 21%</cite>. Long SK Hynix vs Samsung: pure-play memory exposure, <cite index="1-24">UBS predicts SK Hynix will achieve ~70% market share in HBM4 for Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026</cite>, <cite index="5-1,5-2">Samsung shipped HBM4E samples in late May, 20%+ faster than HBM4</cite> but lagging qualification. SK Hynix at inflection; Samsung catching up but de-rated on diversified conglomerate structure and HBM certification delays.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="1-11">BofA forecasts global DRAM revenue to surge 51% and NAND 45% YoY in 2026, with ASPs rising 33% and 26% respectively</cite>. <cite index="4-6,4-13">Analysts believe this cycle is different as AI infrastructure growth consumes hardware at unprecedented rates</cite>. <cite index="8-9">AI will consume 20% of total DRAM production in 2026</cite>. <cite index="8-1,15-7">Memory shortages could persist until 2027 or 2028, with meaningful capacity expansion unlikely until late 2027</cite>. <cite index="16-5,16-6">Samsung and SK Hynix (70% of global DRAM) signaled no aggressive capacity expansion, prioritizing profitability over volume</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-15">BofA estimates 2026 HBM market at $54.6B, up 58% YoY</cite>; <cite index="1-16">Goldman Sachs forecasts HBM demand for ASIC-based AI chips will skyrocket 82%, accounting for one-third of the market</cite>. <cite index="1-18,1-19">HBM3E remains flagship product in 2026, selected by Google, AWS for proprietary ASICs and Nvidia Blackwell Ultra</cite>. <cite index="8-4,8-5">Producing 1 bit of HBM consumes ~3x the wafer capacity of 1 bit of DDR5; HBM has lower yields due to complex packaging</cite>. <cite index="1-20,1-21,1-23">SK Hynix secured world's first mass production system for HBM4 in Sept 2025, expected to support two generations (HBM3E and HBM4) by 2026</cite>. <cite index="5-6">Samsung's customers include AMD, Nvidia, Google</cite>. Micron entering but still sub-scale.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung ships HBM4E samples, 20%+ faster than HBM4
news_pulse.implication: Samsung accelerating HBM roadmap to close gap with SK Hynix; uses 1c DRAM (6th-gen 10nm) + 4nm logic base die. Shares jumped 6.5% on news. Anthropic named Samsung strategic partner.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix Q1 2026 revenue 52.6T won, OP 37.6T won
news_pulse.implication: Record quarterly revenue/profit driven by HBM sales for AI infrastructure. Warns shortages could last until 2027+. Customers reserving supply years ahead.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM Q2 contract +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: NAND now rising faster than DRAM for first time in cycle. Enterprise SSD orders show no sign of slowing. Suppliers reallocating capacity to server/AI, limiting client SSD supply.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler AI capex ~$700B in 2026, doubling from $400B in 2025
news_pulse.implication: Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Alphabet collectively raised capex guidance. 2027 estimates now exceed $1T. Two-thirds of Microsoft capex goes to short-lived assets (GPUs/CPUs, 3-5yr depreciation).

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS gap narrows from 20% to 10% by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS capacity reaching 120-140k wafers/month in 2026 (vs 35k late 2024). Including OSAT partners, total industry capacity ~200k/month. Nvidia holds ~60% allocation.

news_pulse.headline: Foreign investors buy 3.1T won of SK Hynix in 4 days, zero Samsung
news_pulse.implication: Market-cap gap Samsung/SK Hynix narrowed to 2.5x (430T/173T won), closest ever. Pure-play vs conglomerate valuation arbitrage; SK Hynix preferred for AI theme exposure.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix briefly surpasses 2 quadrillion won ($1.3T) market cap
news_pulse.implication: First time crossing threshold. Investors betting on strong earnings, AI memory demand, upcoming ADR listing. Now within striking distance of Samsung as Korea's top stock.

news_pulse.headline: Intel/SoftBank ZAM memory targets 2-3x HBM3 bandwidth at lower power/cost
news_pulse.implication: Zero-Angle Memory presentation at June VLSI conference. 9GB/module (8 layers), 1.6-2.5 GBps bandwidth. NEDO grant approved. Commercialization targeted 2029. Long-term HBM competitive threat.

brief.derivatives_signal: No liquid KRX options data in payload. ADR (HXSCL) illiquid. Monitor KOSPI 200 futures for beta proxy; <cite index="5-7,5-8">Samsung +6.5%, SK Hynix +1.2% on May 29 HBM4E news day vs KOSPI +2.3%</cite> suggests Samsung high-beta to HBM news. Watch for single-stock futures launch post SK Hynix ADR listing.
